This was actually a very common practice at feasts and parties in ancient Rome. They even had a special room in the house for it ... the "vomitorium". People would eat until they were full, then visit the vomitorium and have a slave tickle their throats with a feather until they upchucked. Then they would saunter back into the party and eat some more, later back to the vomitorium, and so on throughout the evening. This seems grotesque to us, but the Romans considered it perfectly normal.

This is a misconception. A vomitorium was not a room to vomit in. It comes from the Latin word "vomo", which means "to go". It was a specialized exit built into the seating of an amphitheater, kinda like how modern stadiums do it. It looks like the English word vomit because they share a root word. Vomitorium -> people exit a stadium, vomit -> bile exits a person. Wikipedia has more info.
